chapters.title: The river engineers assembled
chapters.verdict: The Cooum begins as plumbing: it rises at a junction of surplus channels, receives fresh water only when Poondi reservoir is full, and the tanks it once fed have lost their entire command - the river arrives at the city already spent.

chapters.title: The anicut country
chapters.verdict: The only open water the upstream river holds sits behind ageing structures: Aranvoyal, recorded by WRD as unserviceable after sand mining; Korattur, still exporting Cooum water to Chembarambakkam; and the Paruthipattu check dam, where the restoration programme begins.

chapters.title: Entering the city
chapters.verdict: From Paruthipattu to Koyambedu the mapped river surface reads from orbit as an almost unbroken weed mat - and at Koyambedu the river's consented inflow begins: treated sewage from the plants built to clean it, with industry expressly forbidden from the river on the regulator's own books.

chapters.title: What the measurements say
chapters.verdict: The state measures the Cooum every month and files it to the NGT - BOD 13-24 mg/L across seven locations in May 2026, against a bathing standard of 3 - while the better-known annual series run years behind. The river's freshest public reading is three months old, not three years.

chapters.title: The city channel
chapters.verdict: Through the city the HSCTC survey found the river holding a third to a half of its survey-era width. The interception programme has piped, boomed and fenced much of this stretch, and the plugged outfalls wait on the treatment plants that complete them.

chapters.title: The settled banks
chapters.verdict: The audit record puts 22.7 of 80 bank-kilometres under encroachment in December 2015, with 14,257 project-affected families; by mid-2022 the state had resettled 13,056 of them. The Madras High Court's July 2025 words: the government wants to restore the river, and the project remains struck on account of the encroachments that remain.

chapters.title: The mouth and the sea
chapters.verdict: The mouth has been engineered against the littoral drift since 1998, and PWD's own list records twelve schemes for keeping it open between 1890 and 2000. The current answer - NIOT-designed training walls cleared in 2022 with a mandated three-year fisheries and salinity watch - was reported 40% built in June 2023.

chapters.title: The programme and the money
chapters.verdict: Cooum restoration is a 130-year lineage that has never had more structure than now: Rs 735.08 crore sanctioned and Rs 572.58 crore disbursed, a package-level ledger on the court record, and a global tender announced this month. The nearest precedent is CRRT's own: the restored Adyar creek's faunal count rose from 141 species to about 424.
